name: Galician nationalism
summary: Galician nationalism holds that Galicia is a nation with its own language, culture and history and therefore a right to decide its political future, against the centralism of the Spanish state. Its mainstream, the BNG and the tradition of Castelao, combines this with the defence and normalisation of the Galician language, a secular and republican outlook, strong public services and public control of strategic sectors, feminism, ecology and pacifist anti-imperialism. Its adherents are divided between those who seek independence and those who accept a confederal or federal arrangement.
scope: The contemporary sovereigntist left mainstream of Galician nationalism as represented by the Bloque Nacionalista Galego (charter, XV Assembly documents, 2019 programme), grounded in Castelao's Sempre en Galiza (1944) and the Partido Galeguista. It excludes the Galicianist but non-nationalist currents of the PP and PSdeG, and the reintegrationist and armed fringes, which would answer some language and left-right items differently.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 2019 programme demands universal public health care, an end to co-payments and exclusively public management of core services.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The programme calls for raising the minimum wage progressively to 60% of the average wage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The BNG wants public control of strategic sectors and denounces neoliberal policy, so it rejects the claim that markets beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: The charter backs public control of strategic sectors and the programme proposes a Galician public energy company and public control of the electric system.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The programme attacks tax breaks for big capital and asks for real income-tax progressivity, specific taxes on large profits and large fortunes.

unions-good.rationale: The BNG is tied to the CIG nationalist union and describes itself as defending working people and labour rights.

property-fundamental.rationale: Its programme subordinates property to social ends through public control of strategic sectors, public housing and limits on evictions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The programme seeks public control of energy and credit, bans fracking and wants specific taxes on big companies, which implies tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The programme opposes cuts to public services and demands a social basic income and stronger welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: The BNG backs cooperatives and public participation in the economy, though its documents do not propose general worker ownership of firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: It opposes regressive reforms of civil liberties on the pretext of terrorism threats, so security-justified surveillance is likely rejected.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The XV Assembly lists drug legalisation as a social debate the BNG should take positions on, without stating the position, so a mild yes is inferred from its libertarian-left drift.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The charter commits to opposing discrimination by origin, language, religion or orientation, from which support for legal limits is inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The BNG stresses direct participation and collective self-organisation, and Castelao's liberal-democratic outlook is incompatible with bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: The BNG wants its own sovereign Galician state and a strong public sector, so it holds the state necessary and useful.

limit-guns.rationale: It is a pacifist force committed to combating all forms of violence, from which gun restrictions are inferred, though the sources do not discuss guns.

empower-police-military.rationale: The BNG calls itself anti-militarist and wants the Spanish army and police out of Galician affairs, while proposing its own Galician police.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Feminist and rights commitments pull in opposite directions on this and the sources give no position.

decide-locally.rationale: It demands that decisions be made in Galicia rather than Madrid and stronger municipal powers, though the claim of 'as local as possible' is not its main thrust.

rehabilitation.rationale: Its commitment against all forms of violence and for social justice suggests support for rehabilitation, which the sources do not address directly.

traditional-family.rationale: The charter commits to feminism against heteropatriarchy and to LGBTI rights, which departs from the traditional-family framing.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The charter commits to defending LGBTI rights and fighting discrimination by sexual orientation and gender identity.

abortion-legal.rationale: The programme asks to remove restrictions on voluntary interruption of pregnancy and bans public funding of anti-abortion groups.

more-religion-public.rationale: The charter demands religious neutrality of administrations and the programme asks for secular schools with no religion class.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by origin and ethnicity and backs the rights of dominated peoples, but racial redress is not a Galician theme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The charter's feminism targets heteropatriarchy and non-heterosexual rights, implying a constructionist view, though it never says so.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The charter and programme centre the right to live in Galician and develop Galician culture and the full normalisation of the language.

gradual-change.rationale: The BNG presses for a rupture with the 1978 regime and sovereignty, though it works through institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The programme asks for an asylum-respecting migration policy and addresses root causes rather than restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: It invokes the UN Charter on self-determination but is wary of the EU and NATO, so views on empowering international bodies split.

free-trade.rationale: The programme opposes international trade treaties that harm sovereignty and social, labour and environmental rights, and the BNG opposes the EU model.

nation-first.rationale: The charter describes the BNG as patriotic and internationalist at once, and Galicia's own interests come first but not against global solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The programme rejects imperialist interventions and stresses non-interference and peaceful settlement of conflicts.

open-borders.rationale: The programme wants asylum rights and renegotiated Schengen terms but no open borders, so the sources give no clear answer.

limit-growth.rationale: The charter backs sustainable development but not limits on growth, and the BNG also wants industrial development.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The programme includes a fracking ban, energy control and environment protection, and the Galician nationalist leaders say they face climate change.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The programme backs innovation for quality jobs but offers no general technological optimism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The programme denounces nuclear waste dumped off Galicia's coast and the BNG has an ecologist line, so nuclear expansion is rejected.

revolution-justified.rationale: The BNG pursues sovereignty by democratic means and pledges to combat all forms of violence, including political violence.

experts-over-public.rationale: The charter prefers real democracy with direct participation of the whole population.

central-planning.rationale: It wants public control of strategic sectors but not an economy run entirely by central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: It combines public control of strategic sectors and public banking with a mixed economy, so markets with public or social ownership fit.

land-value-tax.rationale: The programme has no land-tax proposal; its fiscal agenda is progressive income and wealth taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The programme asks for taxes on large fortunes and a progressive system, consistent with heavy taxes on large inheritances.

basic-income.rationale: The programme asks for a basic social income, but it is not shown to be unconditional, and the XV Assembly lists basic income only as a topic for debate.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The programme defends Galicia's productive sectors and a Galician space of free decision on trade, which implies protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme calls for public orientation of productive and strategic investment, public banking and public control of strategic sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme defends smallholders and fishing and farming sectors yet also public and cooperative ownership, so it is split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The BNG seeks an advanced social model within a Galician republic, not the end of money and wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The programme wants public banking and public orientation of credit, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: It wants a Galician framework for labour relations with unions, but not state-recognised bodies that fix wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: The charter describes a democratic, participatory ideal, and the BNG competes in plural elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The charter aims at a republican state and the XV Assembly states the BNG's republican convictions, rejecting institutional respect for the Monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The charter aims at a real democracy based on direct participation and treats democracy as central.

direct-votes.rationale: The charter and programme endorse direct participation and binding referendums, including on self-determination.

workers-councils.rationale: The BNG favours a democratic parliamentary republic rather than councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The BNG holds that Galicia is a nation and so has the right to self-determination, with Castelao calling its denial tyrannical.

natural-rulers.rationale: The BNG's democratic and egalitarian charter rejects the idea of born rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The charter commits to combating all forms of violence, including political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Implied by the BNG's pacifism and its call for disarmament and the end of military blocs; no source addresses war as a builder of character.

separate-church-state.rationale: The charter demands a secular state and religious neutrality, and the programme proposes a secular education system.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The charter demands a secular state with administrations neutral on religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The BNG wants public services and a Galician police and judicial police under public control.

military-superiority.rationale: The BNG is pacifist, anti-militarist, and wants NATO dissolved and arms exports curbed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by origin or ethnicity, and Galician nationalism defines the nation by culture and language, not ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The BNG calls itself a popular nationalism defending working people, but it does not adopt class conflict as the one engine of history, and it holds a range from social democrats to communists.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The programme stresses reducing inequality and guaranteeing rights to housing and work, though it never states equality of outcomes as an aim.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The BNG backs self-determination of peoples broadly, from which sympathy to indigenous authority is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: It is anti-imperialist and neocolonialism is blamed for mass migrations, but the sources do not mention reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: The BNG favours cooperation of peoples with lusophone ties but not political union by religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The charter defends solidarity and the interests of working people, rejecting self-interest as a moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The charter stresses rights and participation and opposes discrimination, not duty-first communitarianism.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The charter commits to the defence of the land and ending animal abuse, and the programme has an animal-protection section.

limit-population.rationale: The BNG worries about demographic decline and emigration, so it opposes limiting population growth.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The charter wants sustainable development within an advanced society, not rejection of industrial civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The programme backs innovation but not disruptive acceleration, and stresses public control.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources are silent on this and left-wing positions are divided.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The charter favours direct citizen participation, not automated government, though the sources do not address it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The BNG opposes regressive curbs on civil liberties on antiterrorist pretexts, which suggests support for strong encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: The charter aims at an advanced model of society, progressive and forward-looking.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The BNG is strongly ideological in its programme and strategy, with a defined project of sovereignty and social emancipation.

direct-action.rationale: The BNG works mainly through elections and institutions while using the street to amplify social struggles.

means-match-ends.rationale: The charter's commitment to peaceful, democratic methods and the fight against violence implies matching means and ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The charter aims at an advanced model of society and sustainable economic development, not a return to hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The BNG does not seek this utopian aim and proposes ordinary labour-rights reforms.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Its parts range from social democrats to communists, and the charter prioritises guaranteeing basic rights rather than a need-based distribution principle.

production-for-use.rationale: The charter backs public control of strategic sectors, not a general end to production for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The coalition includes communists and social democrats, and the sources do not state a theory of profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The charter commits to democracy, participation and rejecting all forms of violence.

collective-farming.rationale: The programme supports the primary sector and family smallholdings, not forced collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The programme blames imperialism and transnational capitalism for conflicts, but does not claim the inevitability of war.

taxation-theft.rationale: The BNG demands more progressive taxation to fund public services.

harm-principle.rationale: The charter commits against discrimination and violence but does not state a harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The BNG's core claim is the collective right of the Galician nation to self-determination.

conscription.rationale: The BNG is pacifist and anti-militarist, so it opposes compulsory military service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from the charter's emphasis on democratic participation; the sources never weigh exit against voice.

state-as-business.rationale: The programme defends public services as pillars of society against marketisation.

positive-liberty.rationale: The charter prioritises guaranteeing health, education, housing and work as material conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: The BNG's critique of power targets the Spanish state and economic elites rather than media and universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by ethnicity and sees no biological basis for ability gaps.

organic-representation.rationale: The BNG is a party that seeks representation through elections and party politics.

total-state.rationale: The BNG is a democratic and participatory movement committed to rights and plural society.

national-rebirth.rationale: Galician nationalism speaks of national recovery and self-esteem, but not of decadence needing a radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The charter rejects domination of some nations over others.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The charter calls for a democratic republic, wholly at odds with oaths of personal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from the charter's defence of labour rights and rejection of domination; bound labour is never discussed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The sources do not address epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources do not address it, though the charter invokes human rights.

single-common-good.rationale: The BNG defends the interests of working people and the popular classes, accepting that interests compete.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The programme condemns Israel for occupation and colonialism and recognises a Palestinian state, though it does not deny Israel's existence.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The programme seeks to make Galician emigrants' return easier, which suggests support for such a right.

revive-national-language.rationale: Galician is already in use, but the programme calls for it to be the preferred language of the administration and for full normalisation.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The charter's participatory-democracy ideal and defence of workers supports a say for workers and the public in company decisions.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme demands a single public education network and denounces diversion of public money to private schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The programme criticises austerity and calls for public investment, so it rejects avoiding stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: The charter prioritises social rights and public control of strategic sectors over economic freedom as a condition of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The BNG favours democratic law and institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: The charter states that Galicia is a nation and therefore has the right to self-determination, and the BNG applies the principle to other nations.

force-without-un.rationale: The programme rejects interventionist policies and asks the Spanish state to withdraw troops from foreign missions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources do not state this, though the BNG is secular.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The programme calls for respect for asylum, social rights and a Galician approach to migration, not welfare restricted to citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The BNG opposes workfare and seeks a social basic income and stronger protections.

class-collaboration.rationale: The BNG is a popular and working-class nationalism favouring organised labour.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The charter prizes Galician culture and its heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: The BNG backs solidarity among peoples against imperialism, including with Catalans and Basques, and with the Saharawi and Palestinians.

workers-nation.rationale: The BNG calls itself patriotic and internationalist while organising workers within the Galician national frame.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The charter commits to feminism against heteropatriarchy.

ban-interest.rationale: The programme proposes public banking and credit, not a ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by origin and ethnicity.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The BNG sees the Spanish state as centralist and neoliberal, but sources do not endorse a general ruling-class theory of the state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme bans fracking and calls for public energy control and environmental protection.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by origin and defends minority language and culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: The programme blames neocolonial policies and war for migration and calls for asylum rights.

proportional-representation.rationale: The BNG, as a minority party, has in its programme asked for improved democracy and a Galician electoral law, but the sources do not describe proportionality.

national-mission.rationale: The charter rejects the domination of some nations over others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The charter frames feminism against heteropatriarchy and violence against women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The programme denounces political parties of the Spanish state and its neoliberal austerity, and complicity of the state with tax fraud.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from the charter's rights-based, anti-discrimination principles; the sources do not discuss eugenics or limits on reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The BNG demands historical memory and the restoration of Castelao's government against the Francoist coup and its repression.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The BNG supports public services and public control of strategic sectors.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred from the charter's opposition to discrimination by origin and ethnicity; the sources never discuss intermarriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The charter opposes all discrimination and calls for equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The sources do not address this Marxist debate.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The programme condemns Israel's occupation and colonialism, but the broader claim is not stated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The charter wants secular state neutrality, but the sources do not address religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The charter holds that administrations should be neutral on religion and opposes religious discrimination.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The animal-rights section targets bullfighting and circuses, not cattle slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The programme says religion will not form part of the school curriculum and demands secular public education.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The sources do not address it and the BNG's own aim is a democratic republic.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The charter bases sovereignty and legitimacy on the will of the Galician people, who should decide freely through direct democracy.

trade-surplus.rationale: The programme opposes trade treaties and mercantile aims and seeks economic sovereignty for Galicia, though not trade surpluses specifically.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from the charter's opposition to discrimination by origin and ethnicity; population transfers are never discussed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The charter commits against all forms of violence, including state violence, but the libertarian absolute is not part of its programme.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The charter stresses solidarity and cooperation between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The sources say little, though the BNG opposes restrictions on civil liberties and was itself targeted by party bans on Basque nationalists.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The charter rejects domination of some nations over others, an analogue of non-domination, though it does not apply the republican concept to persons.

separated-powers.rationale: The BNG seeks a democratic republic, and complains of judicial and state tutelage over Galicia.

vanguard-party.rationale: The BNG's participatory, pluralist model rejects a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The BNG calls itself a popular nationalism prioritising the interests of working people and the popular classes.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The programme wants a public housing stock and a housing pool, favouring public ownership over sales.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The BNG backs workers' rights and unions and opposes regressive labour changes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programme blames structural, economic and imperial causes for poverty and migration.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by origin or ethnicity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The BNG favours direct participation by election and referendum.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The programme opposes regressive reforms of civil liberties under anti-terror pretexts.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The programme calls for action on prices of basic goods such as housing, food and energy.

party-controls-media.rationale: The charter seeks a democratic society, and the programme wants Galician public media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The BNG is anti-militarist and democratic.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The programme supports migrant rights and asylum.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The XV Assembly stresses austerity and the rebellious role of public offices, which fits modest pay, but the sources do not set a rule.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The BNG is a coalition with internal discipline, and its assembly documents expect representatives to follow decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The BNG criticises the current EU as serving globalisation, but Castelao envisioned a federated Europe.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The BNG is republican, parliamentary and anti-militarist.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The BNG demands secular neutrality and takes no position favouring church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: The charter demands a secular state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The programme rejects imperialist wars but the sources do not address this stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The charter commits to cultural rights and democracy.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The charter describes a democratic republic with participation and does not endorse indefinite incumbency.

recall-officials.rationale: The charter's emphasis on direct participation by the whole population supports recall mechanisms.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The programme calls for exit from NATO and dissolution of the alliance, and the withdrawal of troops from foreign missions.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The programme proposes updated tenancy law and public rental housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: The BNG is pacifist and seeks disarmament.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The programme supports the rural world and repopulation but does not make the moral claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Some reintegrationists seek closeness with Portugal, but the mainstream does not claim Galicia and northern Portugal should unite.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The charter defends public education and the BNG draws many members from teachers and intellectuals.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The charter stresses equality among nations and peoples and rejects domination of some by others.

death-penalty.rationale: The charter commits to combating all forms of violence, including state violence.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The programme asks for gender equality and sex education in compulsory education and teacher training.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The programme demands secular education without religion in the curriculum.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Feminist currents divide on this and the sources are silent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The programme wants migrant rights and facilitates return of emigrant descendants, so the sources are mixed.

minority-language-support.rationale: The BNG seeks normalisation of Galician in schools and public services and defends Galician speakers elsewhere.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The charter's secular, neutral state suggests general law applies equally.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The charter's opposition to discrimination and its feminist and LGBTI commitments imply tolerance for non-conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The programme's anti-imperialist stance and its criticism of neoliberal austerity suggest sympathy for debt relief.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The charter pairs national sovereignty with social emancipation and an advanced social model.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The BNG rejects the 1978 constitutional regime and seeks a sovereign Galician republic, which implies a new democratic constituent process.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The charter commits to democracy and rights.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The programme calls for development of peoples and attacks neocolonial plunder, supporting obligations of rich countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The BNG is pacifist and seeks disarmament.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The BNG is republican, though the sources do not specify how the head of state would be chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The programme criticises neoliberal European economic policy and favours public control of credit.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The BNG favours peaceful resolution of conflicts, and the sources do not address the principle.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The charter calls for public control of resources and strategic sectors in service of society.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The BNG draws on several traditions and the sources do not address the question.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The programme bans fracking and opposes nuclear dumping, which fits a precautionary approach.

collective-defense.rationale: The BNG rejects NATO, the main collective-defence alliance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The programme condemns Morocco's illegal occupation of Western Sahara and demands a referendum.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The XV Assembly asks not to favour the Church and the BNG's secular convictions suggest limiting its privileges.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The BNG's republicanism rejects the monarchy that is the usual vehicle for this idea.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Castelao and the BNG hold that denying a nation the right to self-determination is tyrannical, so force against secession is rejected.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The BNG backs a confederation of free nation-states, with Galicia seeking an economic agreement like the Basque one, though it prefers sovereignty.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The BNG is republican and secular.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme calls for real progressivity in income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: The charter's social-justice outlook suggests circumstances shape people, but the sources do not discuss it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The charter commits to democracy and a republican state.

space-expansion.rationale: It is not part of the BNG's priorities.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The BNG seeks a democratic republic based on popular sovereignty.

leader-cult.rationale: The BNG is democratic and republican and stresses collective organisation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Feminist and gender-equality policies exist but the sources do not address custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The sources do not address it.

land-redistribution.rationale: The programme supports small farmers and mobilising unused land, but does not call for confiscating estates.

refugee-return.rationale: The programme backs the Palestinian and Saharawi causes, including return and self-determination.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The BNG claims language rights for Galician speakers in neighbouring Asturias and Castile and León but not territorial annexation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The charter demands secular neutrality and opposes discrimination by religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: The charter's feminism and rights commitments are opposed to compulsory dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: The XV Assembly lists the euro as a debate topic and the BNG criticises EU monetary policy.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Reintegrationists want closeness with the lusophone world, but a political union is not an aim.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The BNG seeks a Galician state, not mere cultural autonomy within one.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The sources do not state the position.

ban-cartels.rationale: The programme targets concentrations of economic power and calls for public control, consistent with breaking up cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: The programme favours public banking and not bank rescue at the expense of the people.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The BNG criticises the tutelage of the constitutional court on Galician autonomy.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The BNG's feminist commitment supports parity in representation, and Ana Pontón is its first woman leader.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme seeks economic sovereignty and a Galician economic space but not isolation from trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The programme opposes treaties that violate social, labour and environmental rights.

moral-incentives.rationale: The sources do not address it.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The charter rejects all forms of violence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The charter seeks a republic and the XV Assembly rejects institutional deference to the Monarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The programme asks that Galician history and culture be taught in a Galician school system.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The charter rejects the domination of some nations over others.

patriotic-education.rationale: The programme asks for a Galician school transmitting Galician language and culture, but not national pride as such.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination, but the sources give no position on racial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: The programme calls for public banking and a public orientation of credit, which fits public money creation only loosely.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The programme criticises transnational capitalism but states no theory of its collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The charter rejects domination and imperialism.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme seeks economic sovereignty and development of peoples, not full delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The sources do not state it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The charter actively opposes discrimination in many forms.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The charter stresses rights, but the sources do not address entrenchment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The programme backs self-determination of peoples such as the Saharawi, which suggests agreement with voiding imposed partitions.

elective-rulers.rationale: The charter aims at a democratic republic.

minority-veto.rationale: The BNG favours democratic participation and referendums, not individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The sources do not address it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The BNG seeks a democratic republic based on popular sovereignty, which implies a supreme parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The charter commits to ending animal abuse and the programme has a section for defence of animals, including a ban on bullfighting.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The programme protects animals but includes the primary sector, with the sources not stating a position on use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The BNG favours rights and redistribution over charitable duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The BNG is an activist movement calling for political participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The sources do not address it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The sources do not address it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The programme blames neocolonial policies and plunder of resources for poverty and migration.

native-born-offices.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by origin.

party-own-road.rationale: The sources do not address it, though the BNG stresses its own path.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The programme stresses development of peoples free of dependence but also aid and solidarity.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The BNG rejects territorial claims by force.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The BNG's charter opposes ethnic privilege.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The BNG denounces the Francoist coup and demands historical memory, treating anti-fascism as foundational.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The BNG condemns Francoism firmly but includes communists, so it is unlikely to equate fascism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: This is not a Galician issue, but the BNG's anti-discrimination charter points against it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The BNG demands historical memory about Francoism, which suggests removing honours for condemned figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The charter's feminism centres women's discrimination.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The charter treats violence against women as structural heteropatriarchal violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The sources do not address it.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The BNG calls itself anti-militarist and refuses institutional deference to the Spanish army.

paid-care-work.rationale: The programme calls for public care services and feminist economy, though not directly for paying domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: The sources do not address it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The programme wants public control of energy and strategic sectors and Galician decisions over key companies.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Its feminist and secular commitments suggest support, though divorce law is not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The charter's direct participation ideal supports binding mandates and recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The programme calls for stronger public pensions and valorisation of pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme protects small landholders and communal lands, but not a general rule of use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: It is a democratic republican position though not discussed.

single-official-language.rationale: The BNG seeks Galician as the preferred language but accompanies it with Spanish, and opposes Castilian-only policy.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The programme defends control of Galician resources, but it does not call for such a ban.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The sources do not address it.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The XV Assembly names the unsustainability of the current consumption model as a theme.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The programme rejects interference and arms sales to belligerents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The BNG upholds sovereignty and non-interference of peoples.

corporate-influence.rationale: The programme criticises the state's complicity with big capital in tax rules.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The BNG champions sovereignty but opposes restrictions on civil liberties.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The programme targets the demographic crisis through support for families, work and emigrant return, and the BNG faces depopulation.

residents-only-property.rationale: The programme contains housing and territorial measures, but the sources do not mention such a limit.

job-guarantee.rationale: The charter prioritises guaranteeing work for all and the programme calls for public employment and job creation.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not address the thesis.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The sources do not address it.

non-intervention.rationale: The programme holds sovereignty and non-interference as principles and condemns imperialist interventions.

industrial-unions.rationale: The sources do not address it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by religion and ethnicity.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The sources do not address it, and the BNG supports marriage equality.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The charter calls for real democracy with participation, which depends on transparency.

local-production.rationale: The programme reinforces Galicia's primary sectors, fishing, farming, and food sovereignty.

informal-organisation.rationale: The BNG is a structured national front with permanent organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The programme insists the Spanish state respect the UN Charter and international law on self-determination.

religious-nation.rationale: The charter's national definition is civic and its state secular.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The charter rejects the domination of some nations over others.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The programme demands a Galician economic agreement like the Basque one so Galicians collect and decide on their own taxes.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The sources do not address the distinction.

defeat-communism.rationale: The BNG includes communists and rejects bloc confrontation.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The programme demands direct public management of essential services against privatisation.

religion-illusion.rationale: The BNG is secular but does not state a theory of religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The sources do not address it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The charter links feminism with an advanced model of society and critique of heteropatriarchy.

socialized-care.rationale: The programme calls for public home care and municipal early-childhood schools.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The BNG seeks language normalisation but it does not propose purging words.

treaties-binding.rationale: The sources do not address it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The charter does not propose small cooperative communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by origin.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The BNG leans left and its charter does not describe a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The sources do not clearly address it, and the BNG backs self-determination of peoples.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination and the BNG is anti-fascist.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The charter commits to defending LGBTI rights.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The BNG is democratic and participatory.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The charter requires religious neutrality of the state.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The BNG is secular and pacifist.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The BNG demands a secular state and rejects violence.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The charter describes the BNG as aiming at a real democracy based on direct participation of the entire population.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The charter links feminism, LGBTI rights, anti-discrimination and working-class interests.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The charter commits to defending LGBTI rights, including gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: The programme calls for decriminalising euthanasia and medically assisted suicide.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The BNG places itself on the left in a popular nationalism.

alienated-labor.rationale: The sources do not state a theory of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by religion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The charter bases authority on popular sovereignty in a secular state.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The charter demands state neutrality but the sources do not address dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The charter's feminist commitments support it, but the sources do not address it.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme combines market elements with strong public control, short of a social market model, and may be more left than that.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The BNG calls itself pacifist and seeks disarmament, but proposes no immediate abolition.

rich-first.rationale: The BNG's egalitarian approach rejects this principle.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The programme calls for exit from NATO and dissolution of military blocs.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The programme wants public banking and new participation formulas, but not user-owned banks at cost.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The XV Assembly denounces EU austerity and cites the Greek case as showing peoples must recover decision-making; it does not discuss lender conditions as such.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The charter combines feminism with defence of the environment and the land.

reification.rationale: The sources do not address it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The sources do not address it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The charter's democratic stance suggests rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by ethnicity.

online-participation.rationale: The charter's direct participation ideal supports it, but the sources do not mention online tools.

open-government-data.rationale: Real participatory democracy suggests transparency, though not discussed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination on religion and origin.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The charter's direct participation ideal is compatible with it, but not stated.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The sources do not address it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The programme criticises tax breaks for big capital and the power of large fortunes.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: It supports LGBTI rights and fights discrimination, but the BNG is anti-militarist.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The charter calls for religious neutrality, not state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The BNG proposes a Galician police and judicial police.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The programme builds on public services and universal rights.

term-limits.rationale: The sources do not address it.

vote-delegation.rationale: The sources do not address it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: It is not a BNG theme.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The charter's feminism supports it though the BNG is secular and religious affairs are outside its scope.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The programme supports migrants' social rights and participation.

rent-control.rationale: The programme asks for reform of the tenancy law and for capping rents.

abolish-ip.rationale: The sources do not address it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The BNG is pacifist and anti-militarist.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Implied by the BNG's demands for disarmament and the dissolution of NATO; the sources cited do not address basing nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The programme calls for leaving NATO and ending foreign military missions.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The BNG backs historical memory and the rights of peoples, but the sources do not discuss such recognitions.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The programme favours taxing capital income more and labour income less.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The BNG is pacifist in outlook but does not espouse absolute non-resistance.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Galician nationalism looks to a long history of Galicia, but the sources do not state a thesis of unbroken continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sources do not address it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources do not address it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Galician nationalism honours its martyrs, with Castelao's album Galiza mártir and the commemoration of Bóveda.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The BNG is secular and materially focused.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The programme seeks return of emigrants and links with the diaspora, with no doctrine of a cultural centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Early Galicianism put culture first but the BNG pursues both language and sovereignty together.

god-not-male.rationale: The sources do not address it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The sources do not address it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by ethnicity.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The BNG wants Galician speakers in Asturias and León to be linguistically protected, but the sources do not say they should merge.

independent-unions.rationale: The BNG is tied to the independent nationalist CIG union.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The sources do not address it.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The programme demands direct public management of essential services.

second-chamber.rationale: The sources do not address it.

municipal-property.rationale: The BNG backs public ownership at national and municipal level, not exclusively community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The BNG proposes a confederation of states, rather than municipal confederalism.

family-wage.rationale: The programme seeks decent wages but the sources do not use the family wage concept.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The programme prioritises public health with no deregulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The sources do not address it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The sources do not address it.

online-anonymity.rationale: The BNG opposes regressive curbs on civil liberties, which supports pseudonymous participation.

person-over-state.rationale: The charter's rights emphasis suggests it, but the BNG also asserts the collective right of nations.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The BNG is secular and the sources do not address it.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The XV Assembly says autonomy as granted is mere administrative decentralisation and insufficient, and demands real sovereignty.

gm-crops.rationale: The programme's environmentalism and support for local farming suggest scepticism, though not stated.

dense-cities.rationale: The sources do not address it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The charter opposes discrimination by ethnicity.

racial-pride.rationale: The charter is civic rather than ethnic.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The BNG is pacifist and rejects imperialist aggression.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Language is central to Galician nationalism and Castelao called it the key to cohesion, though Galicia's own territory defines the nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: The charter opposes religious discrimination and demands a secular state.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The BNG is not paranoid about foreign plots.

free-public-college.rationale: The programme demands lower fees and universal public education from 0 to 18, with access for students on low incomes.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The programme calls for environmental protection but does not specify polluter-pays taxes.

future-generations.rationale: The charter commits to sustainability and defence of the land.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not address it.

arms-reduction.rationale: The charter commits to world peace and disarmament.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The charter's democratic ideal suggests it, but the sources do not address it.

capital-controls.rationale: The programme asks for Galician control over its savings and credit, and the BNG criticises deregulated capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's pacifist, democratic charter, which rejects armed politics; the sources do not discuss private militias directly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the pacifist anti-imperialism of the charter and Castelao's pacifism; conscientious refusal is not stated as a duty.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the left-wing programme's emphasis on wages and workers' rights; sector bargaining is not spelled out in the sources opened.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the programme's support for higher wages and redistributive taxation, though it favours wages and public services over credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The XV Assembly documents criticise EU austerity and its fiscal constraints, which implies opposing legally binding borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The charter's anti-imperialism and solidarity with peoples of the south imply favouring a fairer international economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The BNG is a reformist electoral party seeking sovereignty by democratic means, not the destruction of state institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the programme's public control of strategic sectors, which assumes a set economic direction rather than open experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the charter's ecologism and public-interest framing of natural resources, which resists pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: The charter treats the nation as a civic and cultural community in a secular, republican framework, not a sacred one.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the programme's support for free public education; student loans are marginal in Spain.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Galician nationalism has long described Galicia as subordinated to and drained by the Spanish centre, the basis of its critique of centralism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the humanist rights language of the charter; the sources do not address human nature or enhancement.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from support for public services and promoting the Galician language, for which public broadcasting is a main tool.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The BNG is secular and its documents take no position on whether religions share one truth; inferred as neutral.

farm-price-support.rationale: The BNG programme backs public support for the primary sector and rural Galicia; inferred from that and not a specific price-guarantee demand.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The BNG is pacifist and anti-militarist and opposes NATO, so it favours disarmament over holding nuclear weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: The BNG is a left nationalist front that positions itself with working people, though it is itself a cross-class national party; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: The charter commits the BNG to feminism and women's rights, from which a ban on FGM follows; the practice is not discussed directly.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The charter's feminism implies equal legal property and inheritance rights for women.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The mainstream BNG treats Galician as Galicia's own language and is split with the reintegrationist fringe, which the scope excludes, on whether it is part of a single Galician-Portuguese language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The BNG favours public control and regulation of strategic and environmental matters, not private tort liability instead of agencies; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The BNG is republican, secular and favours direct democracy, so unelected customary chiefs in lawmaking are alien to it; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The charter commits the BNG to ecology and sustainability as a guiding principle, ahead of private interests.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The BNG left programme favours social and rehabilitative justice over fixed harsh sentencing; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Normalising Galician is central to the BNG, but it also welcomes migrants; it would favour learning Galician as part of integration rather than a strict requirement; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's labour-left orientation and its ties to the Galician union tradition, which favour union security.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's stress on expanding participation and rights; the programme sources do not discuss voter ID.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the charter's secular outlook, which favours equal treatment of beliefs by the state.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's emphasis on popular sovereignty and the right to decide, which goes beyond competitive elections alone.

premarital-sex.rationale: The programme's feminist and secular outlook supports women's sexual autonomy.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's defence of civil liberties and digital rights.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the programme's demand for strong public services and public management rather than replacing them with cash.

women-suffrage.rationale: The charter's feminism commits the movement to full equality of women in political life.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the BNG is secular and feminist but the sources do not claim religion is a main cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the charter's anti-racist, internationalist outlook.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The programme's feminism includes public equality policies and institutions.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the BNG's left programme stresses public control of strategic resources and common goods, not first-claim ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The BNG's pacifist anti-imperialism condemns aggression, but the sources I used do not mention criminal courts, so this is inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The BNG's charter describes a secular outlook, so literal scriptural authority is not part of the mainstream.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The BNG charter and programme place feminism at the centre, so guaranteed gender equality in any self-government is expected.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the BNG favours public control of strategic sectors within a mixed economy and democracy, not a bureaucratic planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the BNG's republican and democratic outlook favours direct popular election.

national-church-status.rationale: The BNG's secular outlook rejects special legal status for the Catholic Church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Galician nationalism claims self-government for a nation with its own language, and the BNG sees territorial self-rule as the minimum for national groups.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's insistence that peoples have a right to decide their own political future.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the BNG does not address post-colonial borders, and the anti-imperialist line gives no clear answer.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the BNG's ecology stresses sustainability, but sources do not call for simple, self-sufficient lives.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the BNG's inclusive civic nationalism welcomes people who live and work in Galicia, which cuts against restricting settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the BNG's pacifism opposes compulsory military service, so it would not extend it to women.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The BNG charter defends Galicia's land, language and ecology as a national heritage, though not in mystical terms.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the BNG's human-rights and pacifist outlook.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed in the BNG programmes; inferred as indifferent.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Galician emigrant communities are supported, but no minority-in-neighbouring-states doctrine; adherents split.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's public control of strategic sectors and ecological commons.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the charter's emphasis on rights and freedoms.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No stated position on consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The 2019 programme demands universal public services rather than means-tested provision.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the charter's participatory democracy and party-based pluralism.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the programme's public-interest economy and anti-corruption stance.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The charter is secular and republican, so politics should not run on religious lines; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; the BNG favours modernization with Galician culture, inferred as indifferent.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the BNG's feminism and equality demands.

national-resource-control.rationale: The programme demands public and Galician control of strategic sectors such as energy.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The BNG programme demands strong progressive taxation and public control of strategic sectors, treating the pattern of wealth as a matter of justice, not only of process.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The BNG criticises EU austerity and favours taxing wealth, which suggests support for a levy on speculative finance; inferred, as the cited documents do not name this tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: A left, anti-racist and feminist movement would see structural obstacles as persisting; inferred, since the sources do not address this question directly.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Castelao and the BNG stress the right to resist an unjust centralist state but the sources do not take a position on natural-law doctrine about unjust laws.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The BNG programme favours public services and shorter working time and wages that allow decent lives; support for automation sharing gains is inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Castelao's international federalism, pacifism and the BNG's anti-imperialism favour a balance among peoples over a dominant power; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The sources do not discuss the labour theory of value; the BNG is a broad left-nationalist front and not committed to Marxist economic doctrine.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The BNG charter joins defence of the Galician nation and language with a programme of social justice and public services for working people.

material-over-identity.rationale: The charter gives feminism, language and national identity equal weight with social goals, so it rejects putting identity issues second; inferred from the charter's range.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The BNG is a pluralist, democratic and republican movement that favours direct democracy, and sees markets as subordinate to public control; inferred, not stated about party-led socialism.

missingStatements.text: Nations that share a territory or peninsula should join in a voluntary confederation of sovereign states rather than live in one unitary state.
missingStatements.rationale: The XV Assembly names a confederation of free nation-states or independence as the only routes to sovereignty, and Castelao's final programme moved from autonomy to federation and an Iberian confederation.

notes: The movement splits between autonomists and pro-independence currents; the BNG formally aims at a sovereign Galician republic but accepts a confederal alternative. Most answers on issues the BNG documents address (public services, secularism, NATO, language) are well documented, while many cultural and philosophical items are inferred and marked low. Castelao's own text was read only through secondary summaries and a BNG leaflet.
